verdict.rationale: Typesense's own docs describe it as a typo-tolerant search engine with typo-tolerant keyword search, so typo tolerance is a core, default capability. Its ranking-and-relevance guide includes a dedicated 'Tuning Typo Tolerance' section, and a community user praises its fuzzy text matching. Missing for 10: details of the specific tunable typo/fuzzy parameters (e.g. thresholds, per-field or length-based rules) beyond a section heading, and hands-on corroboration of how the tuning behaves.

support.subject: As a developer, searches tolerate typos and misspellings out of the box, with tunable rules for when and how fuzzy matching applies

citations.quote: Typesense is an open-source, typo-tolerant search engine optimized for instant (typically sub-50ms) search-as-you-type experiences
Typesense combines typo-tolerant keyword search with direct vector search, hybrid search, semantic search, and geo search.
Love the instant search queries and the fuzzy text matching.
